Hedra launches Model Factory for physical-AI post-training and deployment

Hedra launched Model Factory on November 10 for teams building task-specific models from their own data. It combines GPU sandboxes, researchers and AI agents for post-training, evaluation and serving, including robotics and manufacturing teams without internal research labs.

GlobeNewswire / Hedra ↗10 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Infrastructure plus researchers

Hedra launched Model Factory on November 10 for teams building task-specific models from their own data. It combines GPU sandboxes, researchers and AI agents for post-training, evaluation and serving, including robotics and manufacturing teams without internal research labs.

An evaluated improvement loop

Customers bring data and simulators; Hedra helps build datasets, learning environments and evaluations. Production performance informs retraining, with releases described as conditional on passing customer evaluations. People and acceptance criteria remain involved; this is not an unsupervised robot repairing itself.

The robotics result is simulated

A gripper-swap study restored near-zero success to near 100% without policy retraining by matching reach and grasp points in wrist-camera views. It was simulation, not a field result. The separately advertised roughly sixfold speedup concerns image editing with an adapted model, not robot operating speed.
